exercises.name: Barbell Flat Bench Press
exercises.muscle_targeting_notes: The mostly horizontal arm path emphasizes the sternocostal fibers while the full pectoralis major contributes.
instructions: Set the bench or machine angle and adjust the seat/handles so the grips begin around mid-chest for the stated emphasis.
Adjust the seat so the grips begin around mid-chest and the elbows do not travel far behind the torso.
Plant the feet, brace gently, and draw the shoulder blades into a comfortable stable position; grip with wrists stacked over forearms.
Lower the handles or weights under control toward the chest, keeping elbows at a comfortable angle and forearms aligned.
Press along the equipment’s natural path until the arms are nearly straight; keep the ribs down and avoid bouncing or forceful lockout.
common_mistakes: Using a load or resistance that changes the intended path or causes momentum.
Letting shoulders shrug or roll forward at the bottom of the repetition.
Bouncing at the bottom, shortening every repetition, or forcing an uncomfortable stretch.
Holding the breath for repeated reps instead of breathing steadily.
safety_cautions: Stop for sharp pain, numbness, unusual shortness of breath, or dizziness; ordinary muscular effort is different from joint pain.
Set rack safeties just below the lowest controlled bar position; do not rely on collars as a substitute for safeties.
Use a spotter or safety arms for challenging barbell presses; secure benches, anchors, bands, and suspension points before loading.
Keep the load within a pain-free shoulder range and use a lighter variation if control is lost.
People with a current injury or relevant medical condition should follow advice from a qualified clinician.
